advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Rename `jira_raw`/correct the _description_forms docstring to say it matches the inbound-MAPPED Jira value (jira_emit), not the raw snapshot value.
evidence: inbound_differ.py:209 `jira_emit = jira_val` where jira_val is `jira_mapped.get(local_field)` (line 185) and None->"" normalized (line 188-189)
inbound_fields.py:66 `jira_raw: Any,` and docstring lines 79-80 'if it matches the RAW Jira value, treat the field as unchanged'
_map_jira_to_local_fields:279 normalizes description via _normalize_jira_body, so the mapped value is not the raw snapshot body
advisory.finding: In _description_forms the parameter named `jira_raw` and the docstring's claim that the landed form is matched against 'the RAW Jira value' are inaccurate: the caller passes `jira_emit`, which is `jira_val` AFTER `map_remote_to_local` mapping and None->"" normalization (inbound_differ.py:185-189,209-212), not the raw Jira snapshot value. On Cloud this is harmless because the landed form is an ADF dict that cannot equal the mapped plaintext, but the misleading name/comment invites a future change that trusts it to be the raw value.
scenarios: A maintainer later relies on jira_raw being the pre-mapping Jira value (e.g. an ADF dict) and reasons incorrectly about the _text_matches comparison

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting the trailing-whitespace tolerance boundary of the landed-form echo compare (echo differing only by trailing whitespace is suppressed; a non-whitespace edit is not).
evidence: inbound_fields.py:58-60 `if isinstance(a, str) and isinstance(b, str): return a.rstrip() == b.rstrip()`
test asserts only `edited = _to_wiki(_MD) + "\nh2. An operator edit on the Jira side\n"` — a whole appended line, never a trailing-whitespace-only delta
ABSENCE: no test where jira_raw == landed.rstrip() + trailing whitespace, so the rstrip tolerance on the landed compare is uncovered
advisory.finding: The landed-form echo suppression path uses trailing-whitespace-tolerant comparison (_text_matches rstrips both sides, inbound_fields.py:88-93), but no test exercises a Jira value that differs from the local body's landed wire form only by trailing whitespace. A genuine Jira-side edit consisting solely of added/removed trailing whitespace on the rendered wiki would be suppressed as an echo; the negative tests (test_inbound_still_emits_a_genuine_jira_side_edit) only cover an edit that appends a whole new line, so this suppression-vs-real-edit boundary is untested.
scenarios: Jira operator (or a re-render) alters only trailing whitespace of the stored wiki body

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that invokes compute_inbound_mutations with only one of inbound/outbound mapper supplied and asserts the resolver produces the correct configured pair.
evidence: inbound_differ.py:632-635 `if inbound_mapper is not None and outbound_mapper is not None: return ... ; from rebar.config import load_config; from rebar_reconciler._backend_registry import select_backend`
test calls to compute_inbound_mutations pass both `inbound_mapper=_IdentityInboundMapper(), outbound_mapper=_LossyOutboundMapper()`
ABSENCE: no test calls compute_inbound_mutations with outbound_mapper omitted (or inbound omitted) to exercise the resolver fallback
advisory.finding: The new _resolve_backend_mappers partial-injection branch (inbound_mapper XOR outbound_mapper supplied → the other resolved via load_config()/select_backend) is untested. Every test supplies BOTH mappers or NEITHER-of-both is only tested at _diff_jira_vs_local level (which does no resolution); the only compute_inbound_mutations calls pass both mappers, so the registry-seam fallback added in this diff never executes under test.
scenarios: A direct caller omits one mapper; the resolver must fetch the other from the configured backend and yield a consistent pair
